thread:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] 5xx & timeout spike detected in apac-south edgepool (edgepool-apac-south). error_rate=12% over 3m, p99 latency up 4x. incident_id=INC-2026-0421. paging: praveen
praveen: taking this — joining the page. grabbing dashboards now. who has the runbook link?
marta: I have it open: #runbooks/edgepool-degradation. staying on until handoff.
alex: ingress-eng here. seeing a sawtooth pattern on proxy accept queue for edgeproxy-2/edgeproxy-3. conn_backlog ~ 8k and SYN retries spike. also seeing Redis K/V cache misses spike (ttl churn). attaching quick logs:
```
edgeproxy-2 logs:
2026-04-21T09:12:03Z ERROR gateway: upstream timeout route=rgw-apac-south id=abcd status=504
2026-04-21T09:12:05Z WARN connmgr: accept_queue=8123 backlog=7981 fd_wait=120
2026-04-21T09:12:07Z INFO cache: miss_rate=0.78 ttl_evictions=234
```
praveen: thanks alex. is this isolated to apac-south or across APAC?
alex: appears concentrated in apac-south edgepool nodes. eu/na edges look healthy.
evan: tagging platform - possible NAT gateway saturation on that region. we've seen similar when ephemeral port exhaustion happens. checking cloud metrics.
ingress-bot: autopilot-suggestion: shift 30% traffic from edgepool-apac-south -> edgepool-apac-standby for 15m, enable circuit-breaker backoff for clients > 5s.
praveen: doing controlled steer now. running rollout command: `routectl steer --from edgepool-apac-south --to edgepool-apac-standby --percent 30 --sticky false`
praveen: steer accepted, watching p95/p99.
marta: also increasing proxy_connection_timeout from 30s -> 45s on apac-south to reduce mid-request retries. applying as feature flag so we can revert quickly.
jordan: cs here — which customers are impacted? any VIPs? need to prepare a short note.
alex: initial filter shows 24 customer tenants with elevated 503/504, top 3 by error volume: tenant-omega, tenant-lumen, tenant-mkt. API surface area mainly /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.
jordan: prepping comms: short status + mitigation steps. will post to status.redwood.ai (draft): "We detected elevated errors in APAC south; traffic being shifted; mitigation in progress. No data exposure. More updates in 30m."
praveen: quick experiment: restarted edgeproxy-2 container pod on node apac-2b to drain backlog. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/edgeproxy-2 -n edge`
praveen: restart succeeded but CPU spiked on apac-2b during pod pull -> causing short window of higher 5xx for sticky sessions. reversed via stickiness flag.
alex: looking at NAT metrics — ephemeral ports used ~ 92% on apac-south-nat-gw-1. platform: can we scale NAT or add SNAT pool?
evan: raising capacity now. spinning up an extra nat-gw instance and increasing ephemeral port range for that VPC. ETA ~ 6m.
ingress-bot: detected correlation: cache-ttl churn increased after autoscaler event at 08:55. suggestion: throttle autoscaler for distributor service to avoid cache warmup storms.
praveen: good catch. throttling autoscaler -> set min_replicas to 4 for distributor in apac-south.
marta: error rate dropping to 6% after steer + nat scale change. p99 improving but still above baseline.
jordan: posted initial status update to status.redwood.ai and DM'd top affected customers.
alex: rolling a small config change: enable prefix-KV local caching on edgeproxy-3 to lower backend load. applying now.
praveen: summary so far: root cause likely combination of ephemeral port saturation on regional NAT + cache TTL churn after a scaling event -> proxy backlog -> elevated 5xx and timeouts. mitigations: 1) traffic steer to standby pool (30%), 2) scale NAT and expand ephemeral ports, 3) restart/reconfigure edgeproxy with local kv warm caches, 4) throttle autoscaler for distributor.
jordan: CS will wait for 30m update then send targeted customer follow-ups.
evan: NAT capacity up, new gw provisioned, port utilization falling to 45% within 4m.
praveen: flagging a potential longer-term action: add health-based autoscaling cooldown and local warming job post-scale to avoid cache stampede. logging as follow-up item.
ingress-bot: automated test: `curl -i https://apac-south-gateway.redwood.ai/v1/health` -> 200 OK, p95 response 320ms.
marta: handing off to praveen's on-call shadow @jordan in 10m. I need to leave for scheduled rotation, but will remain reachable.
praveen: thanks. @jordan please take lead for the next hour and coordinate post-incident follow-up. I'll stay as advisory.
jordan: taking over. actions for next hour: monitor error_rate < 1% target, confirm cache warm-up across edges, draft postmortem skeleton, list customers notified.
alex: leaving two logs and a short playback for postmortem: `/var/log/edgeproxy/apac-south/rotate-2026-04-21.log` and `proxy-metrics-09-12-14.json`.
praveen: labeling incident INC-2026-0421 as "partial regional degradation" — severity: P2. scheduling postmortem meeting in 72h.
jordan: quick note for comms: "Mitigations applied; monitoring continues. Root cause suspected: regional NAT port exhaustion + cache warm-up after scale; full analysis underway."
customer-success: will update the customer-facing template with above. want any additional technical notes to include?
evan: add that we performed a controlled traffic steer and increased NAT capacity; no data integrity issues.
praveen: closing active page. if anything spikes again, re-open or escalate to platform. good job team :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 status: mitigated -> monitoring. page cleared.
jordan: note for follow-up: assign action items in backlog: 1) autoscaler cooldown, 2) warming-job, 3) nat-scaling-runbook, 4) enhanced edgepool telemetry. I'll create tickets now. thanks all.
